# UI Vault — full catalog

> 1980 entries from 19 sources. Generated by `npm run llms`.

## Sources

### React Bits — https://reactbits.dev
134 free MIT components across text animations, backgrounds, animations and interactive components, with TypeScript/JavaScript and Tailwind/CSS variants per component. Pro tier adds blocks and templates.
License: MIT. Install: npx jsrepo add react-bits/<Component>.
### Motion Primitives — https://motion-primitives.com
~35 minimalist motion components by ibelick, built entirely on Motion (motion.dev). Every component is a copy-paste primitive with a dedicated CLI. Pro adds 50+ premium components and sections.
License: MIT. Install: npx motion-primitives@latest add <name>.
### FancyComponents — https://fancycomponents.dev
~46 fun and weird components recreating effects from award-winning sites — letter swaps, gravity, elastic lines, gooey filters. Fully MIT and open source by danielpetho.
License: MIT. Install: pnpm dlx shadcn add @fancy/<component>.
### NumberFlow — https://number-flow.barvian.me
The animated number (odometer/digit-spin) component. Dependency-free custom element + Web Animations API, reduced-motion aware, SSR friendly. 7.7k GitHub stars.
License: MIT. Install: npm i @number-flow/react.
### Watermelon UI — https://watermelon.sh
Fully open-source shadcn-style library: components, animated micro-interactions, section blocks and 10+ complete dashboards. Free forever for personal and commercial use.
License: Free. Install: npx shadcn@latest add https://registry.watermelon.sh/r/<name>.json.
### Aceternity UI — https://ui.aceternity.com
200+ production-ready components and blocks that "look expensive" — parallax heroes, beams, shaders, docks. Free tier covers ~100 components; premium adds 200+ blocks and full templates.
License: Freemium. Install: npx aceternity-ui@latest add <name>.
### shadcn/ui — https://ui.shadcn.com
65 Radix-based primitives — every install vendors the source into your project — plus 12 OIDC configuration entries from the official @oidc registry (policy form, settings page, 8 provider forms). Charts via Recharts, tables via TanStack, drawer via Vaul, carousel via Embla. The de-facto foundation most libraries below build on.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add <component>.
### Magic UI — https://magicui.design
76 animated components — animated beams, globes, marquees, device mocks, 18 text animations and 11 backgrounds. Distributed as a shadcn registry; templates are paid, all components are free.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add @magicui/<component>.
### Animata — https://animata.design
154 published motion components across text, widgets, cards, bento grids, buttons and heroes — every one installable through a shadcn-style registry. The repo documents 198; 44 are still unpublished.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add https://animata.design/r/<name>.json.
### Animate UI — https://animate-ui.com
154 animated components in your choice of headless flavor — Radix UI, Base UI, Headless UI or native — plus 11 text animations and 14 effect primitives. All Motion-powered, installed via shadcn registry.
License: Free. Install: npx shadcn@latest add @animate-ui/<slug>.
### Launch UI — https://www.launchuicomponents.com
Free section library for marketing pages — navbar, hero, items, logos, FAQ, CTA, pricing, stats and footer blocks, plus button, badge, mockup, screenshot, glow, fade and glass utilities. React 19, Tailwind v4, Radix.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add @launchui/<block>.
### Origin UI — https://coss.com/origin
The Origin UI legacy snapshot, preserved MIT inside the COSS monorepo after the rebrand: 599 variants across 31 families. Inputs alone ship 59 variants; buttons 54; selects 51.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add https://coss.com/origin/r/<family>.json.
### COSS UI — https://coss.com/ui
55 Base-UI-powered components, 2 hooks and 508 registry particles grouped into 54 families — the current-generation component collection from the COSS team, installed through the official @coss shadcn namespace.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add @coss/<component>.
### Cult UI — https://cult-ui.com
77 MIT components — dithered and liquid-metal heroes, neumorphic and beam buttons, dynamic islands, macOS docks, 3D carousels, WebGL shaders and pixel typography. Cult Pro is a separate paid product; only the MIT repo set is cataloged.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add https://cult-ui.com/r/<name>.json.
### Kibo UI — https://www.kibo-ui.com
40 niche components no other library ships — Gantt charts, kanban boards, contribution graphs, credit cards, story reels, glimpse link previews, relative-time and Tinder-style decks. Fully client-side, no external services.
License: MIT. Install: npx kibo-ui add <component>.
### Bklit UI — https://bklit.com
20 chart types — line, area, bar, candlestick, choropleth, composed, funnel, gauge, heatmap, pie, radar, radial, ring, sankey, scatter, sparkline, sunburst — plus 15 chart utilities (legend, tooltip, brush, trend line, deadline …) and 3 stat-card blocks, installed through the @bklit shadcn registry. Tailwind v4.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add @bklit/<chart-name>.
### pdfcn — https://pdfcn.dev
24 PDF primitives (text, heading, data table, graph, QR code, signature, watermark, page header/footer …) and 20 document templates (invoices, reports, tickets, shipping labels, work orders) — every item ships for both the Takumi and Forme renderers.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add @pdfcn/takumi/<name>.
### Remocn — https://remocn.dev
925 Remotion components: 256 text animations, 124 number animations, 66 product scenes, 59 transitions, 59 shaders, 45 logo stings, 75 UI primitives and flows, 31 caption styles, 100 animated icons and full video templates — installed through the @remocn shadcn registry.
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add @remocn/<name>.
### assistant-ui — https://www.assistant-ui.com
147 AI-chat components — threads, composers, message parts, tool UIs, reasoning, attachments, model pickers, voice — in two tiers: 36 runtime-bound components and 111 props-driven elements. The de-facto standard chat-UI library (Vercel AI SDK, LangGraph and more).
License: MIT. Install: npx shadcn@latest add https://r.assistant-ui.com/<name>.

- **Caption Cube** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-cube — Each new phrase turns into view as the next face of a 3D cube, the previous phrase rotating up and away on a horizontal hinge. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Dim Progress** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-dim-progress — The whole phrase sits on screen dimmed and each word brightens the moment it is spoken, with no motion at all. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Drop** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-drop — Each word falls into place from above and bounces as it lands the moment it is spoken, and the whole phrase drops out of frame when the speaker pauses. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Emoji** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-emoji — An emoji pops up above a chosen word the moment it is spoken and stays until the phrase leaves. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Handwrite** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-handwrite — Each word is inked in by hand from left to right at the pace it is spoken, every word sitting at its own slight angle. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Highlight Box** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-highlight-box — A solid box travels behind the word being spoken, sliding from word to word as the voice moves on. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Karaoke** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-karaoke — Transcript captions where each word fills with colour left to right exactly as it is spoken, the whole phrase readable before the voice reaches it. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Knockout** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-knockout — A solid plate with the words cut clean through it, each word punching out the moment it is spoken so the footage shows through the letters. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Label Maker** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-label-maker — Each phrase is punched letter by letter into a strip of embossing tape at the pace it is spoken, the tape feeding out as the words arrive. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Marker** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-marker — Plain captions where the words that matter get a highlighter swipe the moment they are spoken. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Outline** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-outline — Heavy-stroked captions that stay readable over any footage, with the spoken word switching to a contrast colour and nothing else moving. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Prosody** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-prosody — Word size follows the delivery, so drawn-out words land large and rushed words stay small, and the rhythm of the voice is visible with the sound off. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Redact** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-redact — The whole phrase starts blacked out like a declassified file, and each bar pulls away the moment its word is spoken. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Rise** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-rise — Each word slides up out of a mask at its baseline the moment it is spoken, with no bounce and no scale. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Scramble** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-scramble — Each word arrives as random glyphs at the moment it is spoken and decodes left to right into the real letters. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Slice** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-slice — Each word arrives cut in two, the top half sliding in from the left and the bottom from the right, locking together the moment it is spoken. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Slot** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-slot — One short line at a time, each new phrase rolling up into place as the previous one rolls out the top. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Speaker** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-speaker — Dialogue captions where every phrase takes its speaker's colour, so a conversation reads like a script. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Split Flap** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-split-flap — Every letter sits on its own flap tile and clatters through a few characters before landing the moment the word is spoken, like a station departure board. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Stack** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-stack — Kinetic captions stacked a couple of words per line, with the keyword of each page set large on its own line. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]

- **Caption Teleprompter** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-teleprompter — The whole transcript scrolls smoothly through a short window with the current line centred, past lines fading above and the next line waiting below. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Caption Timeline** https://remocn.dev/docs/captions/components/caption-timeline — The whole transcript laid out on a scrolling time strip that slides under a fixed playhead, so every pause shows up as space between words. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]

- **Camera Lens** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/camera-lens — Put a scene behind real glass: resolution falls off toward the corners, highlights bloom through the optics, colour fringes at the edges — a screencast that reads as filmed rather than rendered. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **CRT Screen** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/crt-screen — Put a scene behind curved glass: the picture bulges out to the corners, an RGB phosphor mask and scanlines ride the curve, bright areas flood the mask, and the tube falls away into darkness at the rim. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Halftone Print** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/halftone-print — Print a scene onto paper: each colour separates onto its own rotated screen of dots sized by the ink under them, slightly out of register the way a real press runs. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Hologram** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/hologram — Play a scene as a projection: a ghost double shimmers off the image, emission lines structure it, and only what is bright enough carries through the dark volume it hangs in. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Pixelate Region** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/pixelate-region — Cover rectangles of a scene with an opaque mosaic while the rest passes through untouched — redact keys, addresses and personal data before a demo goes out. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Security Cam** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/security-cam — Run a scene through a cheap recorder: macroblocks flatten under a starved bitrate, colour resolution collapses to half the luma, blacks crush and shadows crawl with sensor noise. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Sustained Glitch** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/sustained-glitch — Broadcast corruption held over a scene in scheduled bursts: slices tear sideways, channels split, and blocks fill with picture pulled from somewhere else — then the frame rests clean until the next hit. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **Underwater Ripple** https://remocn.dev/docs/filters/components/underwater-ripple — Hold a scene under moving water: every pixel is read through a layered refraction field that closes on a whole number of cycles, with colour fringing where the water bends hardest. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]

- **UI Resizable** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/resizable — Two panels split by a draggable handle, where the split ratio is a numeric channel plus a handle idle/hover/press channel (dual-channel value-channel deviation). The Resizable renderer is pure (clamped 0–1 ratio, handle scale, grab-ring opacity); useResizableTransition reads the frame and eases both channels — ratio as a numeric lerp, the handle visual from its state presets. Horizontal and vertical splits; 1px divider + centered grip pill with a derived grab ring. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Select** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/select — A select whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the trigger reuses the Button primitive and the reveal panel composes SelectItem rows. The panel fade, scale, lift, and chevron are keyframed presets. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Select Menu** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/select-menu — A vertical option list where exactly one row is highlighted; the highlight bar and left accent slide smoothly between rows. Fully controlled via selectedIndex/state or useSelectMenuTransition. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Sheet** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/sheet — A side panel whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the backdrop dim and right-edge slide-in are keyframed presets, with a close button and a primary action. Self-contained — pair it with the Button as a trigger (see the example). [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Skeleton** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/skeleton — A skeleton→content crossfade whose loading/loaded state is a pure function of the timeline. The Skeleton renderer is pure (reads no frame); only the composed SkeletonBlock shimmer reads it. SkeletonStyle opacities sum to 1 so the box never dims; real children sit in normal flow and the placeholder (a lines/card layout or a custom node) is an absolute overlay. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Skeleton Block** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/skeleton-block — A shimmer placeholder block — a motion atom (spinner pattern). A directional highlight gradient sweeps across deterministically from useCurrentFrame() and loops seamlessly. Configurable width/height/radius/speed and base/highlight colors. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Slider** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/slider — A slider whose fill is a numeric value channel plus a thumb idle/hover/press channel (dual-channel value-channel deviation). The Slider renderer is pure (clamped 0–100 value, thumb scale, grab-ring opacity); useSliderTransition reads the frame and eases both channels — value as a numeric lerp, the thumb visual from its state presets. Muted track + primary range + bordered thumb with a derived grab ring. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Spinner** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/spinner — A deterministic spinning arc that loops on the Remotion frame — a pure motion atom with no state. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Stepper** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/stepper — A horizontal onboarding stepper whose progress is a pure function of a continuous step index (value-channel deviation). Every circle (fill, number, stroke-dash check) and connector (primary fill fraction) derives purely from the float position; useStepperTransition reads the frame and eases position between step indices. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Switch** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/switch — A switch whose checked/unchecked state is a pure function of the timeline; the track fill and sliding thumb are keyframed presets. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Tabs** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/tabs — A tabs widget whose active-tab state is a pure function of the timeline; the sliding indicator, label colors, and panel crossfade are keyframed/derived presets. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Toast** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/toast — A toast notification whose hidden/visible state is a pure function of the timeline. The Toast renderer is a pure function of a ToastStyle (opacity, translateY, scale); useToastTransition eases both the slide-in enter and the auto-dismiss exit. Variants default/success/error change the leading icon and its color. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Toggle Group** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/toggle-group — A segmented control whose active value is a pure function of the timeline; a raised thumb SLIDES between segments (position + width derived from a float indicator offset, no jumps) and the labels crossfade color via mixOklch. The tabs precedent without content panels. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Tooltip** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/tooltip — A tooltip whose hidden/visible state is a pure function of the timeline. The Tooltip renderer is a pure function of a TooltipStyle (opacity, scale, translate); useTooltipTransition eases both the show and the hide. The static `side` prop sets the enter translate axis and the arrow placement. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]
- **UI Typing Indicator** https://remocn.dev/docs/ui/components/typing-indicator — A continuous typing animation: N dots bounce with a staggered sine wave. A motion atom — it reads the frame and takes color, size, gap, and speed props, defaulting to currentColor so it inherits the bubble it sits in. [MIT, live-previewable, category: video]

### Login & Signup (auth)
- **Auth Blocks** https://ui.watermelon.sh/blocks/auth — 13 login/signup/auth layouts — split screens, centered cards, social-first. [Free, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **OIDC Core** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/getting-started — A starter policy form: GitHub Actions and Vercel behind a toggle picker, each form with its own submit. The file is yours — add providers, swap the picker, and wire onSubmit to your storage. The builder at the homepage generates this file for any provider combination. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **OIDC Settings Page** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/save-and-verify — A working settings page: app/settings/oidc renders the policy form, and a server action validates with validateOidcPolicy before saving. Wire the form's onSubmit to savePolicy and replace the console.log with your storage. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **GitHub Actions Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/github — A self-contained form component that emits an OidcPolicy for a GitHub Actions caller: a repository (owner/repo or a pasted URL) and branch/tag/environment scoping with derived audience. Variants: @oidc/provider-github, @oidc/provider-github-zod, @oidc/provider-github-valibot, @oidc/provider-github-rhf, @oidc/provider-github-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-github-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-github-tanstack, @oidc/provider-github-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-github-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **Vercel Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/vercel — A self-contained form component that emits an OidcPolicy for a Vercel caller: team, project, and environment scoping with derived issuer, plus custom audiences via Vercel's OIDC token exchange. Variants: @oidc/provider-vercel, @oidc/provider-vercel-zod, @oidc/provider-vercel-valibot, @oidc/provider-vercel-rhf, @oidc/provider-vercel-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-vercel-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-vercel-tanstack, @oidc/provider-vercel-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-vercel-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **GitLab CI Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/gitlab — A self-contained form component that emits an OidcPolicy for a GitLab CI caller: instance (gitlab.com or self-hosted), group and project, job-requested audience, and branch/tag/environment scoping. Variants: @oidc/provider-gitlab, @oidc/provider-gitlab-zod, @oidc/provider-gitlab-valibot, @oidc/provider-gitlab-rhf, @oidc/provider-gitlab-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-gitlab-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-gitlab-tanstack, @oidc/provider-gitlab-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-gitlab-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **Google Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/google — A self-contained form component that emits an OidcPolicy for a Google service account caller: account email, optional rename-proof unique ID, and audience. Variants: @oidc/provider-google, @oidc/provider-google-zod, @oidc/provider-google-valibot, @oidc/provider-google-rhf, @oidc/provider-google-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-google-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-google-tanstack, @oidc/provider-google-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-google-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **Bitbucket Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/bitbucket — A self-contained form component that emits an OidcPolicy for a Bitbucket Pipelines caller: paste-in identity provider URL and audience from repository settings, plus repository UUID scoping. Note: the discovery document only exists after Pipelines OIDC is enabled and one pipeline has run. Variants: @oidc/provider-bitbucket, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-zod, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-valibot, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-rhf, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-tanstack, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-bitbucket-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **AWS EKS Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/aws — A self-contained form component that emits an OidcPolicy for an AWS EKS workload: cluster OIDC issuer URL, Kubernetes namespace and service account, and audience. EKS is AWS's OIDC workload identity — plain EC2 and Lambda do not mint identity tokens. Variants: @oidc/provider-aws, @oidc/provider-aws-zod, @oidc/provider-aws-valibot, @oidc/provider-aws-rhf, @oidc/provider-aws-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-aws-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-aws-tanstack, @oidc/provider-aws-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-aws-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **Azure Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/azure — A self-contained form component that emits an OidcPolicy for a Microsoft Entra ID workload: tenant, the caller's object ID, optional client ID, and audience. Variants: @oidc/provider-azure, @oidc/provider-azure-zod, @oidc/provider-azure-valibot, @oidc/provider-azure-rhf, @oidc/provider-azure-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-azure-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-azure-tanstack, @oidc/provider-azure-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-azure-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
- **Custom OIDC Provider** https://ui.shadcn.com/oidc/docs/providers/custom — The escape hatch for any OIDC issuer without a dedicated provider: issuer, audience, optional subject, and free-form optional claims, with a warning when a rule would trust an entire issuer. List it last in the providers array — it matches broadly. Variants: @oidc/provider-custom, @oidc/provider-custom-zod, @oidc/provider-custom-valibot, @oidc/provider-custom-rhf, @oidc/provider-custom-rhf-zod, @oidc/provider-custom-rhf-valibot, @oidc/provider-custom-tanstack, @oidc/provider-custom-tanstack-zod, @oidc/provider-custom-tanstack-valibot. [MIT, live-previewable, category: auth]
